intro: Harald Vetter’s complete performance is released under CC BY 4.0 on both IMSLP and Wikimedia Commons. Compare its opening with Grieg’s abridged 1903 disc; the much longer complete performance contains music absent from that side.
question: How does a complete modern performance frame the composer’s abbreviated reading?

sections.mNote: Shared opening material, but not all of it is mapped

sections.label: Expanding first span
sections.mNote: Measured boundary and rising level, not a bar-aligned event

cues.title: The complete piano piece
cues.text: Vetter plays the complete piece rather than the abbreviated version on Grieg’s disc. Listen to the march-like motion of the opening; only 0:21.6–1:56.31 is matched with the composer’s recording.
cues.evidence: IMSLP labels Vetter’s #461777 a complete performance; its displayed opening incipit reads “Tempo di Marcia un poco vivace”: https://imslp.org/wiki/Lyric_Pieces,_Op.65_(Grieg,_Edvard). Exact alignment input bounds are documented separately from the full stream.

cues.title: Weight and spacing
cues.text: In the shared opening passage, compare how melody and accompaniment fall together. The modern recording makes the piano’s attacks easier to separate, but recording fidelity alone cannot tell us how the two players used their fingers or pedals.
cues.evidence: The report places this before the 0:52 measured boundary. The comparison asks about audible spacing, not an unobserved fingering, pedal change or bar number.
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: The first span gathers
cues.text: The piano’s recorded level rises through this part of the opening. Listen to whether the phrase’s forward motion stays continuous as the texture grows more active.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/grieg-wedding-day-vetter-2006.txt: relative level rises from −16.3 dB at 1:05 to about −9 dB at 1:20–1:30; measured onset density also increases. No particular chord is identified.

cues.title: Beyond the shared passage
cues.text: The complete performance moves into a quieter, less densely attacked middle span. Grieg’s abbreviated side cannot stand in for this whole section; the comparison map has already stopped rather than forcing different music to coincide.
cues.evidence: The report shows a marked drop at 2:00, with lower onset density through the middle. Maureen Buja describes the march-like opening and contrasting subdued second section: https://interlude.hk/silver-memories-grieg-wedding-day-at-troldhaugen/. Timing is approximate, not score-aligned.

cues.title: Let the phrase breathe
cues.text: Through the middle section, follow the line over the quieter accompaniment instead of counting only the strongest attacks. The recording’s smaller changes in level can help reveal the contour without establishing a metronome marking.
cues.evidence: The analysis places 3:15 within the lower-onset-density middle span, with a local level withdrawal around 3:20–3:25. No isolated musical event is asserted.
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: Denser attacks return
cues.text: The later span restores more frequent piano attacks after the middle’s more spacious motion. Keep the opening in mind while listening for similarities in phrasing, without expecting its timings to repeat exactly.
cues.evidence: The report marks changes at 4:18 and 4:22; onset density rises from 1.6 at 4:20 to 3.2 at 4:25. This describes a texture change without claiming a bar-exact thematic return.

cues.title: A later broad crest
cues.text: The later passage builds into another sustained high-level span. Compare the shape of this rise with the first large crest, then listen for the way it gives room to the closing music.
cues.evidence: The report’s 5:58 boundary precedes its loudest window at 6:00; level stays high through 6:15. The comparison is within Vetter’s recording, not a loudness ranking against Grieg.

cues.title: Decay belongs to the ending
cues.text: The final span recedes into the piano’s resonance. Let the sound finish rather than treating the last attack as the whole ending; this complete close lies outside the historical-disc comparison.
cues.evidence: The report falls through 6:35–6:50 and measures no further onsets in its final ten seconds. It does not identify a precise pedal release.
